title: Ext-orthogonal families transfer bounded-above acyclicity across an adjunction
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the common module universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], $S$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $\mathcal B$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives, meaning that every object admits a monomorphism to an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Fix additive functors $L:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $T:\mathcal B\to\mathcal A$ with an adjunction $L\dashv T$, and a small family $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ of $S$-module sheaves. Suppose that for every injective $J\in\mathcal B$, every $i\in I$ and every integer $p>0$ one has $\operatorname{Ext}_S^p(E_i,TJ)=0$, where $\operatorname{Ext}_S^p(E_i,F)=H^p\operatorname{Hom}_S(E_i,I_F^\bullet)$ for an injective resolution $F\to I_F^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $P^\bullet$ be any bounded above acyclic cochain complex of $S$-module sheaves [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] whose terms are isomorphic to small coproducts of members of $(E_i)$, with repetitions allowed. Then the termwise complex $L(P^\bullet)$ is acyclic. More precisely, for every injective $J\in\mathcal B$ the adjunction identifies the acyclic cochain complexes
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P^\bullet,TJ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(L(P^\bullet),J),$$
with term $\operatorname{Hom}(P^{-n},TJ)$, respectively $\operatorname{Hom}(L(P^{-n}),J)$, in degree $n$ and differential $h\mapsto(-1)^{n+1}h\circ d^{-n-1}$. No exactness of $L$ and no injectivity of $TJ$ are assumed.

proof.text: Fix an injective $J\in\mathcal B$. Apply [lem-trf-acyclic-coproduct-ext-orthogonal-hom] with $R=S$, $F=TJ$ and $K^\bullet=P^\bullet$. Its small-site and universe hypotheses are those of the item; its Ext vanishing, bounded-above acyclicity and small-coproduct term hypotheses are precisely the assumptions here. It gives acyclicity of $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P^\bullet,TJ)$ with exactly the degree convention and differential in the statement.

proof.text: Write $\eta$ for the adjunction unit. For each $X\in\mathcal A$ the adjunction bijection $\alpha_X:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B}(LX,J)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(X,TJ)$ is $f\mapsto T(f)\circ\eta_X$. This is additive since $T$ is additive and the categories are preadditive [def-sp-abelian]. For $a:X\to Y$, naturality of $\eta$ gives $\alpha_X(f\circ L(a))=T(f)\circ TL(a)\circ\eta_X=T(f)\circ\eta_Y\circ a=\alpha_Y(f)\circ a$. Taking $a=d_P^{-n-1}$ and multiplying by $(-1)^{n+1}$ proves compatibility with the differentials. Thus the inverse degreewise bijections give the stated isomorphism of cochain complexes of abelian groups. The right-hand complex is acyclic by step 1.

source.place: Tag 07AC, lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek, proof of condition (2): Hom-complex adjunction and testing against injectives.

proof.text: Put $C^\bullet=L(P^\bullet)$, $d_C^r=L(d_P^r)$; additivity makes $d_C^{r+1}d_C^r=L(0)=0$. Fix $r$. In the abelian category $\mathcal B$ [def-sp-abelian], let $q:C^r\twoheadrightarrow Q=\operatorname{coker}(d_C^{r-1})$ and $\bar d:Q\to C^{r+1}$ satisfy $\bar d q=d_C^r$. Its kernel $i:H\hookrightarrow Q$ is $\ker(d_C^r)/\operatorname{im}(d_C^{r-1})=H^r(C)$. By [def-sp-enough-injectives] choose a monomorphism $u:H\hookrightarrow J$ with $J$ injective and extend it across $i$ to $v:Q\to J$, so $vi=u$. The map $h=vq$ kills $d_C^{r-1}$, hence is a cocycle in degree $-r$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(C^\bullet,J)$. By step 2 it is a boundary: after absorbing the differential sign there is $g:C^{r+1}\to J$ with $h=g d_C^r$. Thus $vq=g\bar d q$; since $q$ is epic, $v=g\bar d$, and $u=vi=g\bar d i=0$. A zero monomorphism has zero domain, so $H^r(C)=0$. This holds for every integer $r$, proving acyclicity. This kernel/cokernel argument expands the injective test directly from its defining extension property.
